title: backlog.py tidy lists the merged work and agent branches and clean worktrees, and with --apply removes only what close may remove
goal: backlog.py tidy lists every local work/*, worktree-agent-* and orch/* branch fully on the integration main and every clean, process-free agent worktree under the clone, prints why it keeps each other one, and with --apply removes only those, reusing close's helpers (agents are denied git worktree remove and git branch -D, so it runs as a python process like land); a stale work/ID branch no longer makes a worker's checkout -b fail. An agent may run --apply (gate g1). Planted test: a throwaway repo with merged, unmerged, dirty and checked-out branches.

gates.question: May an agent run backlog.py tidy --apply, which deletes local branches and worktrees (agents are denied git branch -D and git worktree remove, so the command runs them as a python process like land), or does tidy only list?
options: tidy only lists; the operator runs --apply
gates.recommendation: tidy only lists; the operator runs --apply
